walls.note: Dendermonde: late-medieval brick wall with four gates (Jacob van Deventer c. 1565), modernised into a bastioned fortress from 1577-78 (Sanderus 1641 shows the 17th-c. form); traced from the Ferraris map (1777) along the main rampart. The Dender runs through the town into the Schelde on the north side; the Waaslandpoort is a bridgehead over the Schelde.

landmarks.y1650: Cloth hall (14th c.) with belfry on the Grote Markt, together with the meat hall; on the UNESCO list of belfries. The Grote Markt was the forecourt of the counts' castle.
landmarks.src: Inventaris Onroerend Erfgoed, 'Historische stadskern van Dendermonde' (id.erfgoed.net/erfgoedobjecten/140019); UNESCO 'Belfries of Belgium and France'

landmarks.y1650: Meat hall on the Grote Markt.
landmarks.src: Inventaris Onroerend Erfgoed, 'Historische stadskern van Dendermonde' (id.erfgoed.net/erfgoedobjecten/140019)

landmarks.y1650: Collegiate church of Our Lady, main bell tower.
Walled beguinage from 1288 on the right Dender bank.
landmarks.src: Inventaris Onroerend Erfgoed, 'Historische stadskern van Dendermonde' (id.erfgoed.net/erfgoedobjecten/140019)

landmarks.y1650: The Dender joins the Schelde on the north side of the town, at the Waaslandpoort; the town's whole history follows from this confluence.
landmarks.src: Inventaris Onroerend Erfgoed, 'Historische stadskern van Dendermonde' (id.erfgoed.net/erfgoedobjecten/140019)
